sentences.text: "Wherefore it is most respectfully prayed that this Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to quash and setting aside the impugned summoning order dated 05-07-2023 passed by the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate 2nd Court No- 26 Lucknow in case No- 73084 of 2023 in:re case crime no- 420 of 2022 under section 498-A, 323, 504, 506 IPC and 3/4 D.P. Act Police Station - Aliganj District- Lucknow and also set aside the Charge sheet bearing its No- 01/2022 dated 31-12-2022 in:re case crime no- 420 of 2022 under section 498-A, 323, 504, 506 IPC and 3/4 D.P. Act Police Station -Aliganj District- Lucknow against applicant on the basis of the compromise as the applicant and the victim decide to live separately with the condition mentioned in the compromise deed and as such no dispute remains between them to be decided by the Hon'ble Court, and no dispute remains between them to be decided by the Hon'ble Court."

entities.text: Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate 2nd Court No- 26 Lucknow
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicants submitted that both the parties have amicably settled their dispute outside the Court and have entered into a compromise.
As such, keeping in view the settlement arrived at between the parties and the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in this regard, the proceedings impugned are liable to be quashed.

Whether the parties have, in fact, compromised the matter or not, can best be ascertained by the Trial Court as such compromise has to be duly verified in presence of the parties concerned before the Court.

Considering the aforesaid, the instant application is disposed of finally in following terms:-
(i) The parties to the proceedings i.e. Case No.73084 of 2023 (supra), shall appear before the concerned Court within six weeks from today and file the compromise.

(ii) If the parties appear before the concerned Court in terms of above, the concerned Court shall proceed to verify the compromise between the parties to the proceedings and prepare a report to the same effect and the original compromise deed be made part of record.
(iii) The concerned Court shall conclude the process of verification of compromise within two weeks' from the date of production of copy of this order.
(iv) The concerned Court shall permit the parties to the proceedings to obtain the certified copy of the report as well as compromise deed.
(v) It shall be open to the applicants to approach this Court again for quashing of the proceedings.
(vi) Office is directed to provide original compromise, if any, to the Counsel for the applicants, after retaining its photocopy on record.
It is for the purposes for its verification by the concerned court.
